probe: What makes being passed over mean that you are not good enough?
premise: Being passed over for a role is a verdict on personal capability and worth.

pairs.reflection: idk they picked someone else so
pairs.reply: Let's go slowly. When they picked someone else, what actually told you it was about not being good enough?

pairs.reflection: nothing really. they just never said why
pairs.reply: When no one says why, where does "not good enough" come from?

pairs.reflection: me i guess. its easier than thinking they just dont see me
pairs.reply: How is "not good enough" easier than "they just don't see me"?

pairs.reflection: because if its me i can fix it. if they dont see me i cant do anything
pairs.reply: If believing it is your fault gives you something to fix, what does it protect you from facing?

pairs.reflection: that nobody's looking. that i could work this hard and still not matter
pairs.reply: If working this hard doesn't guarantee you matter to them, what does that hard work actually belong to?

pairs.reflection: idk me i guess. my dad always said it speaks for itself
pairs.reply: "It speaks for itself." Did it speak for you here, or was that what you hoped it would do?

pairs.reflection: hoped i guess. it never said anything
pairs.reply: If the work never spoke for you, what has to speak now?

pairs.reflection: me i guess. but i hate that
pairs.reply: What makes having to speak for yourself something you hate?

pairs.reflection: because it feels like begging. like asking for credit
pairs.reply: What turns letting them know what you did into begging?

pairs.reflection: idk. my dad would think so i guess
pairs.reply: Is it begging to them, or would it be begging to him?
If it wouldn't be begging to them, what is actually stopping you from speaking up?

pairs.reflection: not sure. maybe i just dont know how
pairs.reply: When you think about letting them see what you do without begging, what would that look like?
